tweets: Most peptide patients don't realize there are two types of compounding pharmacies — and the difference determines what's actually in your vial. Here's why 503A vs 503B matters:

503A pharmacies: physician-specified formulations for individual patients. Your doctor decides the exact peptide, dose, and compounding needs based on your labs/history. This is the clinical standard we use at VendraRx.

503B pharmacies: bulk-produced 'office stock' for hospitals/clinics. Not patient-specific. Often cheaper, but you lose the precision of a formulation tailored to your biomarkers and physician oversight.

The regulatory distinction exists because patient-specific compounding (503A) requires different safety/quality controls than bulk production (503B). One isn't 'better' — they serve different purposes.
